articles.title: Nordic Rune Field
articles.summary: Angular carved rune lines on dark stone, scattered glowing marks with rough chiseled edges. Reads as a fine sparkly brushed sheen; the specks merge into a glittery shimmer in the highlight and the arcs are barely noticeable.
articles.what: Carved Viking runes on dark stone — angular Algiz/Tiwaz/Othala/Eihwaz line geometries 12-22 px Poisson-scattered + 8-14 hero 24-32 px halo-glowing runes + 3-5 red blood-m Up close: Tiny oval specks, about 8-10 px, scattered in loose wavering columns, each a small ring or pit that glints in the highlight. Beneath them very fine curved concentric streaks arc through, visible as dark swirls in the floor reflection, like a circular-brushed disc. From a distance: Reads as a fine sparkly brushed sheen; the specks merge into a glittery shimmer in the highlight and the arcs are barely noticeable. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Gothic & Horror (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: hero panel, sides, hood.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Gothic & Horror", or search for "Nordic Rune Field".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof, doors: wide highlights show the specks
Wheels or round parts suit the arc brushing
No real effect; numbers stay legible.
Subtle light glints in the highlight, a soft sparkly satin
Pairs well with: matte, satin, metallic, flat.
pitfalls: Not Nordic runes: the name and description describe carved runes, but the render shows fine specks and arc brushing
Not straight brushed metal: arcs are curved and specks dominate
Avoid: glow needs dark base, avoid on light colours.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.goal: Layer Nordic Rune Field over a base finish.
examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.
